title: Dedicated affinity decay and hosted fallback sentry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an ‘affinity decay’ mechanism that slowly reduces strict dedicated-region/tier binding for queued requests when dedicated capacity is constrained, paired with a lightweight hosted fallback sentry that enforces tenant-level safeguards (cost caps, model variant whitelists, and per-tenant grace windows). Goal is to reduce failed requests and tail latency spikes during transient capacity pressure while preserving tenant isolation and cost predictability.

Background and motivation:
- Customers on Dedicated expect preferred routing (same region and tier) for latency and data locality. However, under short-term contention we need a principled way to allow safe, bounded spillover to hosted without creating surprising cost or security exposures.
- Existing approaches either fail fast (request rejected) or immediately spill to hosted, both with downsides: increased customer errors or uncontrolled hosted usage.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) New affinity-decay policy configured per tenant that: initial affinity window = X seconds; after X, affinity score decays linearly over Y seconds until spillover eligibility threshold is reached.
2) Hosted fallback sentry that validates three constraints before allowing hosted execution: tenant cost cap not exceeded, model variant is allowed for tenant, and request size/latency budget doesn't violate SLOs.
3) Metrics and dashboards: per-tenant affinity hits, decay-triggered spillovers, rejection counts, cost delta for spillovers, and flow traces linked to request IDs.
4) Controlled rollout: start with 5 pilot tenants, compare error rate and cost delta vs baseline, and auto-rollout rule only after safety gates pass.

Design proposal (implementation notes):
- Affinity scoring: maintain an in-memory score in the dedicated scheduler keyed by (tenant, route, model-variant). Score starts at 1.0 on allocation success; when capacity pressure occurs queueing or preemption events decrement score by configurable steps; otherwise score recovers slowly. When score < 0.6 and queue time > affinity_window, request becomes eligible to consult fallback.
- Decay timer semantics: two knobs: affinity_window (default 2s) and decay_period (default 10s). These are per-tenant and can be overridden by Dedicated customers.
- Hosted fallback sentry checks (in order):
  1) Tenant-level cost budget: compare estimated token cost of spillover to remaining monthly cap; block if >10% of remaining cap or if cap exhausted.
  2) Allowed model variant list: consult tenant allowlist configured in control plane; if mismatch, block and offer a lower-cost compatible variant if present.
  3) Latency budget check: if estimated additional network/serving latency pushes request past SLO, block and queue instead.
- Fallback execution path includes tagging requests with spillover_reason and origin_affinity_score for traceability; trace flows are annotated in Console traces UI.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Simpler approach would be purely time-based queue-to-hosted fallthrough; rejected because it doesn’t adapt to tenant behavior or cost constraints.
- Affinity-decay adds complexity to scheduler state but reduces noisy spillover during short bursts. We accept extra memory per-tenant (estimate ~200 bytes/active-route) because our active-route cardinality is bounded per GPU shard.
- Cost checks may cause false negatives (blocking spillover) for tenants with very tight caps; we will surface a diagnostic that suggests temporary cap increases for pilot customers.

Implementation plan (epics and tasks):
- Phase 1 (PoC) [ENG-90452-A]: implement affinity score plumbing in dedicated scheduler + unit tests.
- Phase 2 (Sentry) [ENG-90452-B]: implement hosted fallback sentry with cost and allowlist hooks; wire to control plane config.
- Phase 3 (Telemetry) [ENG-90452-C]: add metrics, Console traces, and a per-tenant dashboard.
- Phase 4 (Pilot & Rollout) [ENG-90452-D]: run with 5 pilot tenants for 2 weeks, evaluate, then open rollout to progressively larger percentage.

Progress updates and notes (chronological):
- 2026-02-20 (Aisha Patel): Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting with product and infra. Decided to make affinity parameters tenant-configurable.
- 2026-02-25 (Marcus Nguyen): Scheduler PoC completed; in-memory affinity table added, simple linear decay implemented. Unit tests pass locally. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427.
- 2026-03-02 (Marcus Nguyen): Design review with security and product. Security requested explicit audit log entries for all spillovers (done). Product requested a fallback variant ranking to prefer cheaper quantized variants; added to scope.
- 2026-03-05 (PR review): Code review feedback on concurrency: prefer sharded locks for affinity table; Marcus updated implementation. Performance microbench shows <2% scheduling latency regression under 95th percentile load. Bench results: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/bench/ENG-90452/2026-03-05.
- 2026-03-10 (QA): Integration test found an edge: tenants with 0-cap budget previously returned 403; new behavior should queue for retry instead of immediate block to avoid UX regression. Updated sentry to enqueue up to 5s before hard block and emit a diagnostic flag.
- 2026-03-12 (Marcus Nguyen): Metrics added to Console staging. Pilot onboarding doc drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Routing/Affinity+Decay+Pilot. Planning kickoff with two pilot tenants on 2026-03-18.

Rollout plan and rollback criteria:
- Canary rollout to 5 tenants for one week. If spillover error rate increases >5% or cost delta >20% of expected for a tenant, pause and revert affinity-decay for that tenant.
- Hard rollback: disable sentry and affinity-decay flags cluster-wide if we see a system-level increase in failed reservations or queueing > 99th percentile baseline.

Observability and SLOs to track:
- Affinity-to-hosted spillover rate (per-tenant)
- Mean and P95 latency for requests that spilled to hosted vs succeeded on dedicated
- Token cost delta attributable to spillovers (daily and weekly)
- Number of blocked spillovers due to cost or model-allowlist checks

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we expose an API for customers to opt-in dynamic spillover and see simulated cost impact before enabling? (PM leaning yes)
- What is the default decay_period for high-throughput tenants? Need empirical tuning.
- Long-term: integrate with global smart routing to prefer geo-sibling regions with lower latency instead of Hosted when available. This is a follow-up epic.

- PM to prepare rollout communication and update pricing page with guidance for spillover cost implications.
